question: Reports indicate that the Dutch municipality of Nissewaard is making a fishmonger set up and take down his fish stall every day because of new EU rules1. However, the Representation of the European Commission in the Netherlands has stated that these rules were determined by the municipality itself2.

This situation seems to suggest that the Services Directive, which obliges EU Member States to free up the services market, is so complicated that it leads to undesirable situations with negative consequences for social welfare and liveability. In view of the above, could the Commission clarify the following: 1.
How does the Commission assess the Services Directive in terms of simplicity, effectiveness and proportionality from the optic of the situation in Nissewaard?
How often does the Services Directive lead to unnecessary local rules and regulations and if there is no data available on this, is the Commission willing to look into the issue?
If the situation in Nissewaard has not been caused by EU rules, how can such undesirable situations be prevented in the future?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.4.2024) A full chapter of the Directive 2006/1231 is dedicated to administrative simplification, laying down provisions to modernise rules applicable in the Member States with regard to access to, and exercise of, a service activity. This chapter applies no matter whether procedures and formalities are imposed at national, regional or local level.

Implementation of the Directive resulted in hundreds of national laws being modernised and thousands of discriminatory, unjustified and disproportionate requirements being eliminated2. The notification procedure established by the Directive aims to ensure that new national requirements falling under the Directive comply with these simplification and modernisation requirements and to prevent new barriers.

In 2022, to help competent authorities to apply the Services Directive, the Commission updated the Handbook on the implementation of the Services Directive3. Member States have a primary responsibility to monitor the application of the relevant legal provisions and to take the necessary steps for enforcement.

No provision of the Directive requires fishmongers or any other street merchants to set up and take down their stall every day. This is not an obligation deriving from EU law. However, such an obligation, if imposed by a national, regional or local law, needs to be justified by an overriding reason in the public interest and be proportionate to the objective, in accordance with EU law.
1 Directive 2006/123/EC of 12 December 2006 on services in the internal market. Often referred to as the

Services Directive. 2 Communication from the Commission on the implementation of the Services Directive.
